checks.evidence: Review: AST:ALT ratio >1 in 92% and >2 in 70% of alcoholic liver disease; ratio <1 points toward NAFLD/NASH.
Search returned nothing on muscle injury, heart attack or hypothyroidism raising ALT/AST.
Both GGT and ALP rise in liver disease but only ALP rises with bone disease; normal GGT with high ALP suggests bone cause. Exact PMC page ambiguous in blended results.
British Liver Trust: bilirubin forms as the body clears worn-out red blood cells; the liver normally removes it.
British Liver Trust: albumin is a protein made by the liver; level falls if the liver is damaged.
Returned: extrahepatic causes of acute jaundice include gallstone disease, haemolysis, malignancy. Hepatitis, pancreatitis, sickle cell, alcohol not confirmed.
checks.newSentence: Jaundice can have causes outside the liver, including gallstone disease and the breakdown of red blood cells (haemolysis).
